newsitem.title: USA: IBM stock hit by earnings fears, leads Dow lower.
newsitem.headline: IBM stock hit by earnings fears, leads Dow lower.

text.p: The stock of International Business Machines Corp. fell in heavy trading on Thursday, hit by a report that analysts were cutting their 1997 earnings forecasts for the giant computer company.

The sell-off fuelled the overall stock market's fourth sharp sell-off in five days, as investors were already scared that Friday's March employment report, if robust, could prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates again soon.
IBM fell $4.125 to $129.625 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was among the most active issues in late morning trading.
IBM shares began their tumble in London, where investors first read the Wall Street Journal article, which said analysts may not be through cutting IBM's earnings estimates.
As a result, investors worried about what will happen to IBM shares in coming weeks as it nears the release of its first-quarter earnings, due April 23.

"If IBM either misses already reduced earnings estimates or 'talks down' estimates for the second quarter, it could not only take the already badly bruised tech group down even further, but it could also inflict another blow on the market as a whole," the article said.
For the fourth quarter, IBM's profits jumped 18 percent to $2.02 billion from $1.71 billion in the year-ago period. Revenues rose 6 percent to $23.1 billion from $21.9 billion.

While profits were bolstered by strong services and software sales, analysts were disappointed with IBM's sluggish mainframe sales and restructuring costs. The company also managed to meet forecasts by lowering its corporate tax rate.
The report said Morgan Stanley cut IBM's 1997 earnings estimate to $12.30 a share from $12.50.

Dean Witter Reynolds analyst Jay Stevens believes his estimates of $2.25 a share for the first quarter and $2.75 a share for the second quarter are "still too high," but he is reluctant to cut his numbers again since he has already done that several times, the report said.
Last month, Merrill Lynch said it will be tough for IBM's first-quarter earnings, which it estimates at $2.32 a share, to compare with the year-ago period.
At 11:30 a.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was down 37.39 points at 6,479.62 after having fallen as low as 6,434.
